messages:
anna: Heads-up — observed a 15-25% tail latency spike on 1F1B runs for the new kernel-selector rollout (heuristic_v2) on the 8xA40 cluster since yesterday.
mike: Which workload? microbatch size, seq len?
anna: Tied to our long-sequence chat workload (seq=4096). Microbatch=4, pp=8, tp=1. Baseline (heuristic_v1) had steady tails.
li: Do you have traces/prof output? could be all-reduce stepping up or KV cache miss amplification.
anna: Pasting profiling snippet from perf-bot run:

```text
perf-bubble-summary:
  stage_0 compute: 12.1ms
  stage_0 comm   : 0.7ms
  stage_1 compute: 11.9ms
  stage_1 comm   : 0.65ms
  allreduce total: 2.3ms  <-- increased from 0.45ms baseline
  kv-lookup lat   : 0.4ms (hit) / 3.2ms (miss)
  kv-hit-rate     : 62% (was 94%)
``` 

sophie: whoa allreduce x5. That explains PP bubble widening.
perf-bot: alert: kernel-selector=heuristic_v2 triggered kernel_fallback on 3/8 workers; reason: not quantized-friendly GEMM chosen.
mike: kernel_fallback -> more memcpy + rendezvous for allreduce? that explains longer comm windows.
li: Also kv-hit drop from 94->62% suggests KV cache eviction pattern changed. Are we touching cache layout with the new kernel (different memory alignment)?
anna: I did a quick diff: commit 0a1b2c3 updated kernel tiling heuristics and also changed batch packing order. Packing order change could affect prefix reuse -> fewer KV hits.
sophie: quick test idea: revert packing order locally but keep heuristic_v2. If tails go down, packing order is the culprit.
mike: Meanwhile, can we force kernel-selector to prefer quantized kernels as a rollback? `RW_KERNEL_SELECTOR=prefer_quant` on infra side.
li: I ran a micro experiment: reverted packing order -> kv-hit-rate goes back to 93%, allreduce 0.5ms, tails back to baseline. So packing order + kernel fallback combo is the multiplier.
anna: Good find. So two levers: revert packing-order or make kernel-selector avoid fallback by preferring quantized kernels for these models.
sophie: Which is lower-risk for the upcoming deploy window? Reverting packing-order is smaller change and low risk.
mike: Agreed. Also add a guard in selector: if fallback_count > 1 in last 5 mins, auto-revert to previous selector and page.
li: Action items:
  - anna: open PR to revert batch packing change and add e2e test for kv-hit regression (assign to you)  (ETA: today)
  - mike: add rollout guard to kernel-selector (small flag + alert) (ETA: tomorrow)
  - sophie: run wider perf sweep on 8xA40 and 4xA40 after revert (ETA: today afternoon)
  - perf-bot: keep collecting bubble timelines for the next 12h

anna: I'll open PR + link perf traces. Thanks all.
mike: Nice sleuthing. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: perf-trace: https://perf.internal/runs/1963123456 (attached timeline)
sophie: after revert test results look good, will sign off if sweep passes.
li: logging note: let's add a KV cache metric to the runtime telemetry (kv_hit_rate per route) — that would have flagged this earlier.
anna: Agreed. Creating a ticket for telemetry.
mike: moving to patch + monitor. If anything else flares, ping this thread.
